name: ITIL Service Intelligence
description: Business Glossary for the ITIL 5 Accelerator Suite. Defines standard ITIL 5 terminology, conformed field names, KPI definitions, calendar intelligence concepts, and pipeline governance terms used across Service Intelligence, Pipeline Pulse and Conform Data applications.
overview: [{"type": "paragraph", "children": [{"text": "This glossary is the source of truth for the ITIL 5 Accelerator Suite built on Qlik + ServiceNow. It covers: ITIL 5 Core Concepts (Incident, Problem, Change), Conformed Date Fields (the five shared date dimensions that work across all ITSM source systems), Performance KPIs (MTTR, FCR, Change Failure Rate), Performance Flags (the Dual Yes/No fields), Calendar Intelligence (period flags), Record Identity (keys and links), Classification and Routing (shared dimensions), Source Systems (ServiceNow, FreshDesk and beyond), and Pipeline Governance (architecture terms). Terms include Qlik Answers-optimized descriptions with natural language synonyms to enable intelligent routing of business questions to the correct data fields regardless of which source system originated the data."}]}]

terms.name: ⏱️ % of Time in API Call
terms.description: The share of total pipeline run time spent waiting on the source API, used to attribute bottlenecks to a specific stage rather than treating "the pipeline is slow" as one undifferentiated problem. Expression: Sum(meta_api_duration_sec) / Sum(meta_total_duration_sec). Synonyms: API time share, extract bottleneck %, API duration ratio.

terms.name: ⏱️ Avg API Response Time
terms.description: Average time, in seconds, the pipeline spent waiting on the source API call during the extract stage of a run. Expression: Avg(meta_api_duration_sec). The first of five pipeline-stage duration measures (API, Merge, Join, Store, Total) that together diagnose where time is being spent in a run. Synonyms: API duration, extract time, source call time.

terms.name: ⏱️ Avg Join Duration
terms.description: Average time, in seconds, spent performing the inner join step of a pipeline run (associating new/changed records with existing keys). Expression: Avg(meta_join_duration_sec). Third of the five pipeline-stage duration measures. Synonyms: join time, join stage duration.

terms.name: ⏱️ Avg Merge Duration
terms.description: Average time, in seconds, spent merging incremental records into the existing dataset during a pipeline run. Expression: Avg(meta_merge_duration_sec). Second of the five pipeline-stage duration measures. Synonyms: merge time, merge stage duration.

terms.name: ⏱️ Avg Store Duration
terms.description: Average time, in seconds, spent writing the final QVD to disk during a pipeline run. Expression: Avg(meta_store_duration_sec). Fourth of the five pipeline-stage duration measures. Synonyms: store time, QVD write time, save duration.

terms.name: ⏱️ Avg Total Pipeline Duration
terms.description: Governed via two master items: a Total Pipeline Duration master DIMENSION (the raw elapsed seconds for that single run straight from meta_total_duration_sec — use this in row-level tables and detail views, it's the actual figure for that run, not an average) and an Avg Total Pipeline Duration master MEASURE (Avg(meta_total_duration_sec) — averages across whatever runs are in scope, the right behavior for KPIs and trend charts but not for row-level detail). The primary SLA-style measure for pipeline performance. Synonyms: total run time, overall load duration, end-to-end duration.

terms.name: ⏱️ Change Data Staleness (Display)
terms.description: A human-readable rendering of Change Data Staleness (Hours) as "X Days Y Hours Z Minutes," omitting any unit that is zero. Expression: built from Floor(), Hour(), and Minute() applied to the vChangeStaleness load-script variable, with singular/plural handling. DISPLAY ONLY — use Change Data Staleness (Hours) for sorting or thresholds. Synonyms: change freshness label, change lag text, how stale is change data.

terms.name: ⏱️ Change Data Staleness (Hours)
terms.description: The elapsed time, in fractional days, between when the application was last reloaded and when the underlying Change data was last loaded from source. Expression: vLastAppReloadTime - vLastChangeLoad, captured as the load-script variable vChangeStaleness. Use this numeric version for sorting, coloring, and threshold alerts — never the Display variant. Synonyms: change freshness, change lag, change staleness.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Conformed Record Count
terms.description: Row count immediately after all MasterCalendar Left Joins complete in the Conform Data app, before STORE. Should always equal Conform Source Record Count.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Extract Duration
terms.description: Seconds spent reading the raw ITIL QVD for this table in the Conform Data app, before any calendar joins.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Join Duration
terms.description: Seconds spent running all MasterCalendar Left Joins for this table in the Conform Data app. The stage most likely to slow down as the calendar or join count grows -- up to 14 sequential joins per table.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Row Count Delta
terms.description: Conform Conformed Record Count minus Conform Source Record Count. MUST be 0. A nonzero value means a MasterCalendar Left Join fanned out somewhere in that table's calendar-join chain -- almost always a date field name that no longer matches what MasterCalendar expects, causing an unintended Cartesian join. Investigate immediately if nonzero.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Run ID
terms.description: Timestamp shared across all rows produced by one Conform Data reload -- ties the master_calendar/incident/problem/change_request rows together as one run. A different clock than Pipeline Pulse's own Run Date/meta_run_id; the two data islands are not joinable on run identity.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Run Status
terms.description: SUCCESS if Conform Row Count Delta is 0 and Conform Source Record Count is greater than 0; FAILURE otherwise. Cheap automated pass/fail signal for a Conform run without opening the data.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Source Record Count
terms.description: Row count immediately after the main LOAD from the raw ITIL QVD in the Conform Data app, before any MasterCalendar joins. Baseline for the row-count parity check against Conform Conformed Record Count.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Store Duration
terms.description: Seconds spent writing the Conform_*.qvd for this table in the Conform Data app.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Table
terms.description: Which table this Conform checkpoint row describes: master_calendar, incident, problem, or change_request. Sourced from the ITIL Conform Data app's Meta_Conform.qvd, loaded into ITIL Pipeline Pulse as its own data island -- every field is aliased with a conform_ prefix so it shares zero field names with the raw Pipeline_Telemetry table, preventing an accidental associative link between two different "run" clocks.

terms.name: ⏱️ Conform Total Duration
terms.description: Total seconds for this table's Conform pass end-to-end: extract + calendar joins + store.

terms.name: ⏱️ Deleted Record Count
terms.description: Governed via two master items: a Deleted Record Count master DIMENSION (the raw per-run value straight from meta_deleted_record_count — use this in row-level tables and detail views) and a Deleted Record Count master MEASURE (Sum(meta_deleted_record_count), safe at row grain too, but use the dimension for row-level detail for consistency). A non-zero, unexpected spike here is a "silent data loss" tripwire worth alerting on. Synonyms: records deleted, purge count, removed rows.

terms.name: ⏱️ Final Record Count
terms.description: Governed via two master items: a Final Record Count master DIMENSION (the raw per-run value straight from meta_final_record_count — use this in row-level tables and detail views) and a Final Record Count master MEASURE (Sum(Aggr(FirstSortedValue(meta_final_record_count, -meta_increment_start), meta_table_name)) — collapses all runs to the latest snapshot per table, for KPIs and aggregate charts only). CAVEAT: the measure returns blank/zero for most rows if placed in a table already sliced to a single run — always use the dimension for row-level detail. Synonyms: table row count, current record total, final row count.

terms.name: ⏱️ Incident Data Staleness (Display)
terms.description: A human-readable rendering of Incident Data Staleness (Hours) as "X Days Y Hours Z Minutes," omitting any unit that is zero (e.g. "20 Hours 58 Minutes" rather than "0 Days 20 Hours 58 Minutes"). Expression: built from Floor(), Hour(), and Minute() applied to the vIncidentStaleness load-script variable, with singular/plural handling ("1 Hour" vs "2 Hours"). DISPLAY ONLY — never sort, filter, or threshold on this text version; use Incident Data Staleness (Hours) for that, exactly as Priority Sort Order is used instead of Priority for chart axis sorting. Synonyms: incident freshness label, incident lag text, how stale is incident data.

terms.name: ⏱️ Incident Data Staleness (Hours)
terms.description: The elapsed time, in fractional days, between when the application was last reloaded and when the underlying Incident data was last loaded from source. Expression: vLastAppReloadTime - vLastIncidentLoad, captured as the load-script variable vIncidentStaleness. Use this numeric version for sorting, coloring, and threshold alerts (e.g. flag red if staleness exceeds a business-defined SLA) — never the Display variant. Synonyms: incident freshness, incident lag, incident staleness.

terms.name: ⏱️ Load Type
terms.description: Whether a given pipeline run was a FULL reload (entire dataset rebuilt) or an INCREMENTAL load (only new/changed records since the last watermark). FULL runs are expected to show larger record counts and longer durations than INCREMENTAL runs — comparing the two without this dimension in scope will skew duration and volume averages. Sourced from meta_load_type. Synonyms: load mode, full vs incremental, reload type.

terms.name: ⏱️ Max Total Duration (Worst Run)
terms.description: The longest total duration observed among selected pipeline runs — flags outlier/worst-case runs that may need investigation rather than getting smoothed out by an average. Expression: Max(meta_total_duration_sec). Synonyms: worst run time, slowest run, max load duration.

terms.name: ⏱️ New Records Loaded
terms.description: Governed via two master items: a New Records Loaded master DIMENSION (the raw per-run value straight from meta_new_record_count — use this in row-level tables and detail views) and a New Records Loaded master MEASURE (Sum(meta_new_record_count), safe at row grain too, but use the dimension for row-level detail so the table stays consistent with Final Record Count). Reflects incremental load volume; will spike on FULL loads. Synonyms: records added, new rows loaded, incremental volume.

terms.name: ⏱️ Pipeline Table
terms.description: The ITIL 5 record type this pipeline run loaded: change_request, incident, or problem. The primary slicer for all Pipeline Observability measures — lets you see whether load performance and data freshness differ by practice area. Sourced from meta_table_name in the pipeline telemetry (Meta_*.qvd files). Synonyms: table name, load target, practice area table.

terms.name: ⏱️ Problem Data Staleness (Display)
terms.description: A human-readable rendering of Problem Data Staleness (Hours) as "X Days Y Hours Z Minutes," omitting any unit that is zero. Expression: built from Floor(), Hour(), and Minute() applied to the vProblemStaleness load-script variable, with singular/plural handling. DISPLAY ONLY — use Problem Data Staleness (Hours) for sorting or thresholds. Synonyms: problem freshness label, problem lag text, how stale is problem data.

terms.name: ⏱️ Problem Data Staleness (Hours)
terms.description: The elapsed time, in fractional days, between when the application was last reloaded and when the underlying Problem data was last loaded from source. Expression: vLastAppReloadTime - vLastProblemLoad, captured as the load-script variable vProblemStaleness. Use this numeric version for sorting, coloring, and threshold alerts — never the Display variant. Synonyms: problem freshness, problem lag, problem staleness.

terms.name: ⏱️ Run Date
terms.description: A calendar-friendly date derived from the pipeline run's increment start time (meta_increment_start), used to trend run volume, duration, and freshness over time rather than by opaque run ID. Pairs with a calendar/date-spine table for zero-filled daily trending, consistent with the Opened_Date_Spine pattern used elsewhere in the accelerator. Synonyms: load date, run day, pipeline date.

terms.name: ⏱️ Run Status
terms.description: The outcome of a pipeline run — SUCCESS today, with FAILURE/PARTIAL expected once error handling is added to the load script. Currently 100% SUCCESS across all 61 logged runs, so Success Rate will show a flat 100% until failure scenarios exist in this dataset. Sourced from meta_run_status. Synonyms: run outcome, load result, job status.

terms.name: ⏱️ Source File
terms.description: The physical QVD file the pipeline telemetry row was written to — one of Meta_Changes.qvd, Meta_Incidents.qvd, or Meta_Problems.qvd. Useful for troubleshooting at the file level when a specific extract needs review. Sourced from meta_source_file. Synonyms: telemetry file, QVD source, meta file.

terms.name: ⏱️ Success Rate
terms.description: Percentage of pipeline runs that completed with a SUCCESS status. Expression: Count(DISTINCT {<meta_run_status={'SUCCESS'}>} meta_run_id) / Count(DISTINCT meta_run_id). CAVEAT: currently a flat 100% because failure/partial run statuses have not yet been captured in this dataset — this measure earns its keep the day something breaks. Synonyms: run success %, pipeline health, job success rate.

terms.name: ⏱️ Total Runs
terms.description: Count of distinct pipeline executions logged in the telemetry, across all tables and load types. Expression: Count(DISTINCT meta_run_id). The core volume metric for "how many times has this pipeline fired." Synonyms: run count, execution count, number of loads.

terms.name: ⏱️ Visualize Record Count
terms.description: Total ITIL_Facts rows after one Service Intelligence app reload (Incidents + Problems + Changes combined). A basic sanity heartbeat -- this app is a pure consumer with no transform logic, so an unexpected drop to near-zero is the main signal worth watching for.

terms.name: ⏱️ Visualize Reload Duration
terms.description: Whole-script wall-clock duration in seconds for one Service Intelligence app reload. Not broken into stages -- this app is a pure consumer with no multi-step pipeline to time, unlike the raw extract and Conform stages.

terms.name: ⏱️ Visualize Run ID
terms.description: Timestamp of one ITIL Service Intelligence app reload. A different clock than Pipeline Pulse's own Run Date and Conform Run ID; not joinable to either -- three separate data islands, three separate clocks.

terms.name: ⏱️ Visualize Run Status
terms.description: SUCCESS if Visualize Record Count is greater than 0; FAILURE otherwise. Does NOT reflect whether Conform Data itself ran cleanly -- check Conform Run Status for that. This is deliberately a heartbeat, not a borrowed copy of Conform's own health check.

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Change Lead Time
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The average number of days between when a change was requested and when implementation began. Measures change management process efficiency. Expression: Avg([Change Lead Time Days]). Long lead times indicate bureaucratic approval bottlenecks. Short lead times with high failure rates may indicate insufficient planning time. DORA defines Change Lead Time as one of its four key metrics — elite performers achieve lead times under one day. Synonyms: change lead time, time to implement, approval to implementation time, change cycle time.

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Change Lead Time Days (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average Change Lead Time in days (time from request to scheduled/planned start), lifetime/no date restriction. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis instead of flag-multiplication - testing showed 60 of 63 still-active Changes already have a real Change Lead Time Days value (it populates once Scheduled, not once Closed), so a (1-Is Active) denominator was excluding most valid data. Expression: Avg([Change Lead Time Days]) - field only exists on Change rows, so no Record Type filter needed; Avg() natively skips nulls. Trades SQL-portable Sum()/Sum() style for correctness. Synonyms: change lead time, average lead time, request to start time.

linksTo.subResourceName: CHG: Avg Change Lead Time Days (Lifetime)

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Change Lead Time Days CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Change Lead Time Days restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis - the old (1-Is Active) flag-multiplication pattern was excluding most valid data since Lead Time populates at Scheduled, not Closed. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date CMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Change Lead Time Days]).

linksTo.subResourceName: CHG: Avg Change Lead Time Days CMTD

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Change Lead Time Days PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Change Lead Time Days restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis, same fix as Lifetime and CMTD. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date PMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Change Lead Time Days]).

linksTo.subResourceName: CHG: Avg Change Lead Time Days PMTD

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Implementation Duration
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The average number of hours a change implementation took to complete. Measures implementation efficiency and planning accuracy. Expression: Avg([Implementation Duration Hours]). Long implementation durations increase maintenance window risk and operational disruption. Compare planned vs actual duration to assess change planning accuracy. Break down by Change Type to understand which change categories take longest. Synonyms: implementation duration, change duration, how long to implement, deployment duration, change execution time.

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Implementation Duration Hours (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average Implementation Duration in hours (how long the actual change work took), lifetime/no date restriction. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis instead of flag-multiplication - testing showed 2 still-active Changes already have a real Implementation Duration Hours value, meaning the field doesn't populate strictly at closure and a (1-Is Active) denominator was silently excluding valid data. Expression: Avg([Implementation Duration Hours]) - field only exists on Change rows, no Record Type filter needed. Synonyms: implementation duration, average change duration, deployment time.

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Implementation Duration Hours CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Implementation Duration Hours restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis, same fix as the Lifetime version. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date CMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Implementation Duration Hours]).

linksTo.subResourceName: CHG: Avg Implementation Duration Hours CMTD

terms.name: ⚙️ Avg Implementation Duration Hours PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Implementation Duration Hours restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date PMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Implementation Duration Hours]).

linksTo.subResourceName: CHG: Avg Implementation Duration Hours PMTD

terms.name: ⚙️ CAB Delegate
terms.description: The CAB member designated to represent or review this change on behalf of the full Change Advisory Board. Used in organizations where individual CAB delegates are assigned per change rather than full board review. Synonyms: CAB representative, CAB member, change reviewer, board delegate.

terms.name: ⚙️ CAB Recommendation
terms.description: The formal recommendation issued by the Change Advisory Board for this change request. Values: Approved, Rejected, Deferred, Approved with Conditions. CAB Recommendation is the outcome of the CAB review meeting. Only populated for changes that required CAB review (CAB Required = Yes). Synonyms: CAB decision, CAB outcome, advisory board recommendation, CAB approval.

terms.name: ⚙️ CAB Required
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change required Change Advisory Board review and approval before implementation. CAB Required Rate = Sum([CAB Required]) / Count([Change ID]). High CAB rates indicate complex or risky change portfolios. Tracking CAB Required vs Emergency Change reveals governance health. Synonyms: CAB needed, CAB review, change advisory board required, needs CAB approval.

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Risk High Count
terms.description:
Count of active changes with High risk rating. Requires CAB review. Synonyms: high risk changes, how many high risk.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Risk Rating]={'High'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Risk Moderate Count
terms.description:
Count of active changes with Moderate risk rating. Maps to the Medium tier in the Change Risk donut visualization. Synonyms: moderate risk changes, medium risk changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Risk Rating]={'Moderate'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Risk Very High Count
terms.description:
Count of active changes with Very High risk rating — the highest risk tier, typically requiring CAB escalation and executive sign-off. Synonyms: very high risk changes, critical risk changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Risk Rating]={'Very High'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Status Assess Count
terms.description:
Count of changes under initial assessment before authorization. Synonyms: changes being assessed, under review, evaluation stage.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]={'Assess'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Status Authorize Count
terms.description:
Count of changes awaiting CAB or management authorization. A large Authorize count indicates approval pipeline bottlenecks. Synonyms: pending approval changes, awaiting CAB, authorization queue.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]={'Authorize'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Status Implement Count
terms.description:
Count of changes currently being implemented. Synonyms: in progress changes, active implementation.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]={'Implement'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Status Scheduled Count
terms.description:
Count of changes in Scheduled status — approved and awaiting their implementation window. Synonyms: scheduled changes, approved changes, upcoming changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]={'Scheduled'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Total Planned Changes
terms.description:
Total count of all active changes — excludes Closed and Canceled. Primary headline KPI for the Changes dashboard. Includes New, Assess, Authorize, Scheduled, Implement, and Review states. Synonyms: planned changes, active changes, open changes, change backlog, how many changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Type Emergency Count
terms.description:
Count of active Emergency changes — urgent changes that bypass normal CAB approval. A rising Emergency count signals reactive change management. Synonyms: emergency changes, urgent changes, expedited changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Change Type]={'Emergency'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Type Normal Count
terms.description:
Count of active Normal changes requiring full CAB review and approval. Synonyms: normal changes, CAB changes, full approval changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Change Type]={'Normal'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ CHG: Type Standard Count
terms.description:
Count of active Standard changes. Pre-approved, low-risk, repeatable — no CAB required. Synonyms: standard changes, pre-approved changes.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Change'}, [Change Status]-={'Closed','Canceled'}, [Change Type]={'Standard'}>} [Change ID])

terms.name: ⚙️ Change
terms.description: A planned modification to IT infrastructure, services, or processes. ITIL 5 defines Change Enablement as the practice of maximizing the number of successful IT changes by ensuring that risks have been properly assessed and authorized. Changes are classified as Standard (pre-approved, low risk), Normal (requires CAB review), or Emergency (urgent bypass of normal approval). In the Service Intelligence accelerator, Change records originate from ServiceNow (change_request table) and are identified by Record Type = 'Change' in the ITIL_Facts table. Key ITIL 5 KPIs: Change Failure Rate (DORA metric), Change Lead Time, Implementation Duration, CAB Required rate, Emergency Change rate. Conformed date fields: Opened Date (opened_at), Started Date (work_start), Mitigated Date (Null - emergency only), Resolved Date (work_end), Closed Date (closed_at). Synonyms: change request, modification, deployment, release, implementation.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Category
terms.description: The top-level category classifying what type of infrastructure or service domain the change affects. Examples: Hardware, Software, Network, Security, Application, Database. Use Change Category for portfolio analysis — which domains are experiencing the most changes, which categories have the highest failure rates. Synonyms: change domain, change area, what kind of change, infrastructure category.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Failed
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the change caused an incident, required rollback, or was otherwise unsuccessful. Change Failure Rate (DORA metric) = Sum([Change Failed]) / Count([Change ID]). This is one of the four DORA elite performance metrics. Industry benchmark: elite performers have less than 15% change failure rate. Synonyms: failed change, change failure, rollback, deployment failure, change caused incident, DORA change failure.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Failure Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Change Failure Rate — the percentage of changes that caused an incident, required rollback or were otherwise unsuccessful. One of the four DORA elite performance metrics for DevOps and IT performance benchmarking. Expression: Sum([Change Failed]) / Count([Change ID]). DORA benchmarks: Elite performers under 15%, High performers 16-30%, Medium 31-45%, Low performers over 45%. A high Change Failure Rate combined with high Emergency Change Rate indicates reactive and poorly tested change management. Synonyms: change failure rate, DORA CFR, failed change percentage, rollback rate, deployment failure rate.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Failure Rate % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI (DORA): Change Failure Rate - % of Changes that caused an incident or required rollback, across ALL Changes. Lower is better. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Failed]) / Sum([Change Counter]). NOTE (2026-08-10): denominator corrected from (1-[Is Active]) to [Change Counter] — old formula caused null when no changes reached terminal state. This is the DORA Change Failure Rate metric. Synonyms: change failure rate, CFR, failed change rate, DORA change failure rate.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Failure Rate % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI (DORA): Change Failure Rate restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. Uses stored Is NotActive flag. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Failed]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Is NotActive]*[Opened Date CMTD]). Lower is better.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Failure Rate % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI (DORA): Change Failure Rate restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. Uses stored Is NotActive flag. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Failed]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Is NotActive]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ Change ID
terms.description: Unique sys_id identifier for the Change record. Use Count([Change ID]) as the base count expression for all change KPIs. Source field: Change = sys_id (CHG rows only). Synonyms: change sys_id, CHG sys_id, record ID.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Implementer
terms.description: The individual technician assigned to implement this change. Use for individual workload and accountability analysis. Source field: Change = assigned_to. Synonyms: change owner, implementer, who is implementing it, change technician, deployment engineer.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Lead Time Days
terms.description: The number of days between when the change was requested and when implementation began. Raw numeric field behind Avg Change Lead Time KPI. DORA defines this as one of its four key performance metrics. Expression: [Started Date] - [Requested By Date]. Synonyms: lead time, days to implement, approval to implementation days, how long to get approved.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Model
terms.description: A reusable change template defining the standard approach, steps and approvals for a frequently repeated change. Change Models reduce planning effort for routine changes by providing a pre-approved blueprint. Examples: Server Patching Model, Firewall Rule Change Model, Database Backup Model. High usage of Change Models indicates process maturity. Synonyms: change template, change blueprint, change procedure, standard change model.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Number
terms.description: Human-readable change number (e.g. CHG0030001). Use as the display identifier in drill-through tables. Source field: Change = number. Synonyms: CHG number, change reference, change ticket number.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Phase
terms.description: The current phase this change is in during its lifecycle. Change Phase is more granular than Change Status for tracking multi-phase implementations. Examples: Planning, Testing, Deployment, Validation, Rollback. Use to identify changes currently in risky phases like Deployment or Rollback. Synonyms: implementation phase, current phase, change stage, deployment phase.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Scope
terms.description: Defines the breadth and boundary of what this change will affect. Examples: Single Server, Multiple Servers, Single Application, Enterprise-Wide, Network Segment. Change Scope is a key input to risk assessment — wider scope generally means higher risk and greater need for CAB review and rollback planning. Synonyms: scope of change, change boundary, what is affected, change impact scope.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Status
terms.description: The current lifecycle state of a Change request in ServiceNow. Values: New, Assess, Authorize, Scheduled, Implement, Review, Closed. Change Status is more granular than Lifecycle Status for change management reporting — use Change Status when analyzing where changes are stuck in the approval and implementation pipeline. A large count stuck in Authorize indicates CAB bottlenecks. Synonyms: change state, where is the change, change lifecycle, approval status.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Success Rate % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Changes implemented successfully without causing incidents or requiring rollback, across ALL Changes. Denominator = all changes opened in the period (not just closed ones). Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Successful]) / Sum([Change Counter]). NOTE (2026-08-10): denominator corrected from (1-[Is Active]) to [Change Counter] — old formula caused null when no changes reached terminal state. Synonyms: change success rate, successful change rate, implementation success rate.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Success Rate % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Change Success Rate % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. Uses stored Is NotActive flag. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Successful]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Is NotActive]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Success Rate % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Change Success Rate % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. Uses stored Is NotActive flag. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Change Successful]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Is NotActive]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Successful
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the change was implemented successfully without causing incidents or requiring rollback. Change Success Rate = Sum([Change Successful]) / Count([Change ID]). High success rates indicate effective change planning and testing. Synonyms: successful change, change succeeded, implementation succeeded, deployed successfully.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Summary
terms.description: A one-line summary of what this change will do. Primary display label for changes in list views and dashboards. Rich source for Qlik Answers — asking what a change involves will surface the Change Summary. Synonyms: change title, change description, what is the change, change name, what will be done.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change Type
terms.description: The classification of a change by approval requirement and risk profile. ITIL 5 standard values: Standard (pre-approved, low risk, repeatable, no CAB required), Normal (assessed and approved by CAB, moderate to high risk), Emergency (urgent bypass of normal approval, highest risk, post-implementation review required). Change Type is the primary dimension for analyzing change portfolio composition. A rising Emergency Change rate signals reactive change management. Synonyms: change classification, change category type, standard normal emergency, type of change.

terms.name: ⚙️ Change URL
terms.description: Clickable URL linking directly to the change record in ServiceNow. Built in CONFORM layer as [ServiceNow Base URL]/change_request.do?sys_id=[Change ID]. Synonyms: change link, CHG URL, ServiceNow link, open change.

terms.name: ⚙️ Conflict Status
terms.description: Indicates whether this change conflicts with another scheduled change on the same CI or maintenance window. Values: No Conflict, Conflicting. Conflict Status is used by the Change Impact Analysis workflow — any change with Conflict Status = Conflicting requires resolution before implementation proceeds. Synonyms: change conflict, scheduling conflict, conflicting change, maintenance window conflict.

terms.name: ⚙️ Emergency Change
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change bypassed the normal CAB approval process due to urgency. Emergency changes carry higher risk and should be reviewed post-implementation. Emergency Change Rate = Sum([Emergency Change]) / Count([Change ID]). A rising emergency change rate indicates reactive rather than planned change management. Synonyms: emergency change, E-change, urgent change, expedited change, break-glass change.

terms.name: ⚙️ Emergency Change % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Changes classified as Emergency (bypassed normal CAB approval), across all active Changes, lifetime/no date restriction. A rising Emergency Change % signals reactive rather than planned change management. Expression: Sum([Change Counter] * [Emergency Change]) / Sum([Change Counter]). Synonyms: emergency change rate, unplanned change %, emergency change percentage.

terms.name: ⚙️ Emergency Change % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Emergency Change % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with Emergency Change % PMTD. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Emergency Change]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ Emergency Change % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Emergency Change % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot, paired with Emergency Change % CMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Emergency Change]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ High Risk Change
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change was rated High Risk during the risk assessment process. High Risk Change Rate = Sum([High Risk Change]) / Count([Change ID]). High risk changes require additional scrutiny, testing and rollback planning. Correlate with Change Failed to understand whether high risk changes actually fail at higher rates. Synonyms: high risk, risky change, risk level high, elevated risk change.

terms.name: ⚙️ High Risk Change % (Lifetime)
terms.description: RISK KPI: % of active Changes rated High or Very High risk, lifetime/no date restriction. Useful as a leading indicator of CAB workload and potential change-induced incident exposure. Expression: Sum([Change Counter] * [High Risk Change]) / Sum([Change Counter]). Verified 2026-07-29: 41 of 101 Changes are High Risk, consistent with the Change Risk donut's High(19)+Very High(20) breakdown. Synonyms: high risk change rate, risky change %, CAB escalation rate.

terms.name: ⚙️ High Risk Change % CMTD
terms.description: RISK KPI: High Risk Change % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[High Risk Change]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ High Risk Change % PMTD
terms.description: RISK KPI: High Risk Change % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[High Risk Change]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚙️ Implementation Duration Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping changes by implementation duration range. Examples: Under 1 Hour, 1-4 Hours, 4-8 Hours, 8-24 Hours, Over 24 Hours. Use to understand the distribution of implementation durations and identify changes that consistently run over their planned window. Synonyms: duration bucket, implementation time band, how long band.

terms.name: ⚙️ Implementation Duration Hours
terms.description: The number of hours the change implementation took to complete. Raw numeric field behind Avg Implementation Duration KPI. Long durations increase maintenance window risk. Expression: ([Resolved Date] - [Started Date]) * 24. Synonyms: implementation time, how long to implement, deployment duration hours, execution time.

terms.name: ⚙️ Implementation Outcome
terms.description: The documented outcome after the change was implemented. Values: Successful, Unsuccessful, Rolled Back, Partially Successful. Implementation Outcome is the post-implementation verdict that drives Change Successful and Change Failed flags. Rich Answers content — analysts can ask what happened after a change was implemented. Synonyms: change outcome, implementation result, what happened, did it work, change result.

terms.name: ⚙️ Implementation Team
terms.description: The specific team responsible for implementing this Change request in ServiceNow. Change-specific equivalent of Fulfillment Team. In the ITIL_Facts table this field is populated only for Change rows — null for Incidents and Problems. Source field: ServiceNow change_request table assignment_group. Synonyms: change team, implementation group, deployment team, who is implementing.

terms.name: ⚙️ Lead Time Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping changes by lead time range for distribution analysis. Examples: Same Day, 1-3 Days, 4-7 Days, 8-14 Days, Over 14 Days. Use alongside Avg Change Lead Time to understand the distribution of approval times not just the average. Synonyms: lead time bucket, approval time band, lead time range.

terms.name: ⚙️ Outside Maintenance Window
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change was implemented outside its approved maintenance window. Outside Maintenance Window changes are a compliance violation and carry higher risk of unintended impact. Sum([Outside Maintenance Window]) should ideally be zero. Any non-zero value indicates scheduling or change control discipline issues. Synonyms: outside window, outside maintenance, change window violation, off-hours change.

terms.name: ⚙️ Planned End
terms.description: The scheduled end date and time for change implementation. Defines the end of the maintenance window. Compare Planned End against Resolved Date (work_end) to measure whether changes completed within their scheduled window. Changes finishing after Planned End may trigger Outside Maintenance Window = Yes. Synonyms: scheduled end, maintenance window end, planned implementation end, when does it end.

terms.name: ⚙️ Planned Start
terms.description: The scheduled start date and time for change implementation. Defines the beginning of the maintenance window. Use Planned Start with Planned End to identify changes scheduled within a specific maintenance window. Compare Planned Start against Started Date to measure scheduling accuracy. Synonyms: scheduled start, maintenance window start, planned implementation start, when does it start.

terms.name: ⚙️ Production System Change
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change affects a production system directly. Production System Changes require the highest level of scrutiny and approval. Tracking production vs non-production change ratios helps assess operational risk exposure. Synonyms: production change, prod change, live system change, production impacting.

terms.name: ⚙️ Requested By
terms.description: The person who submitted or initiated this change request. Identifies who in the business requested the modification. Use to analyze change demand by requester, department or role. Synonyms: requested by, change initiator, who requested it, change submitter, business requester.

terms.name: ⚙️ Requested By Date
terms.description: The date and time the change was originally requested by the business. The starting point for Change Lead Time calculation. Requested By Date combined with Started Date measures how long it took to move from request to implementation. Synonyms: request date, when requested, change request date, submission date.

terms.name: ⚙️ Review Status
terms.description: The post-implementation review status for this change. Values: Not Required, Scheduled, In Progress, Complete. Post-implementation reviews are mandatory for Emergency Changes and any change that failed or had unexpected outcomes. Review Status = Complete indicates a closed-loop change process. Synonyms: PIR status, post-implementation review, review complete, change review.

terms.name: ⚙️ Risk Rating
terms.description: The assessed risk level of this change request. Values: Low, Moderate, High, Very High. Risk Rating drives the approval path — High and Very High risk changes require CAB review and detailed rollback planning. Correlate Risk Rating with Change Failed to validate whether high-risk changes actually fail at higher rates. Use Risk Sort Order for correct chart axis ordering. Synonyms: risk level, change risk, how risky, risk assessment, risk score.

terms.name: ⚙️ Risk Sort Order
terms.description: Integer sort companion to Risk Rating enabling correct Low-Moderate-High-Very High axis ordering on charts. Values: 1=Low, 2=Moderate, 3=High, 4=Very High. Always use Risk Sort Order as the sort dimension when Risk Rating is the chart axis. Synonyms: risk sort, risk order, risk sequence.

terms.name: ⚙️ Unauthorized Change
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this change was implemented without proper authorization. Unauthorized changes are a significant risk indicator and ITIL 5 compliance failure. Sum([Unauthorized Change]) should always be zero in a well-governed environment. Any non-zero value requires immediate investigation. Synonyms: unauthorized change, rogue change, unapproved change, change without approval.

terms.name: ⚙️ Unauthorized Change % (Lifetime)
terms.description: COMPLIANCE KPI: % of Changes flagged as Unauthorized (implemented without proper approval), across all active Changes, lifetime/no date restriction. Any non-zero rate here is a governance red flag. Expression: Sum([Change Counter] * [Unauthorized Change]) / Sum([Change Counter]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): currently a flat 0% across all 101 Changes - either genuinely clean or the flag has never been triggered in this synthetic data; not yet verified which. Synonyms: unauthorized change rate, unapproved change %, compliance violation rate.

terms.name: ⚙️ Unauthorized Change % CMTD
terms.description: COMPLIANCE KPI: Unauthorized Change % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Unauthorized Change]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]). CAVEAT: flat 0% in the Lifetime version too - unverified whether genuinely clean or never triggered.

terms.name: ⚙️ Unauthorized Change % PMTD
terms.description: COMPLIANCE KPI: Unauthorized Change % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Expression: Sum([Change Counter]*[Unauthorized Change]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Change Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚠️ Assigned Resolver
terms.description: The individual assigned to resolve this incident. Use for individual workload and performance analysis. More granular than ALL: Fulfillment Team. Source field: Incident = assigned_to. Synonyms: assigned to, resolver, agent, assignee, who is working it, owner.

terms.name: ⚠️ Average Response Time Hours (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average number of minutes between an incident's Opened Date and Started Date (when active work began) — the response-time proxy for how quickly incidents get picked up after being logged, lifetime/no date restriction. Expression: Avg([Minutes to Respond]). FIX (2026-08-10): switched from Sum(([Started Date]-[Opened Date])*24) hour-based date math, which floored to whole hours and lost minute-level precision, to a dedicated [Minutes to Respond] field for cleaner display. Started Date (work_start) is now populated on at least some incidents, resolving the prior 0%-populated caveat. Synonyms: response time, time to first response, time to start, pickup time.

terms.name: ⚠️ Average Response Time Hours CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average Response Time in minutes restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month, day-of-month aligned to PMTD for a fair trend comparison). Feeds the "current" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Average Response Time PMTD. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date CMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Minutes to Respond]) — Avg() with Set Analysis, not flag-multiplication. FIX (2026-08-10): switched from hour-based date math to the dedicated [Minutes to Respond] field. Flag-multiplication (Sum(Counter*Field*Flag)/Sum(Counter*Flag)) is unsafe here — incidents not yet responded to have null Minutes to Respond, and the flag-multiplied version silently treats those as zero-minute responses in the numerator while the denominator still counts them, deflating the average (validated: 31 vs correct 38.75). [Opened Date CMTD] stores text 'Yes'/'No', not 1/0. Synonyms: current month response time, this month pickup time.

linksTo.subResourceName: INC: Average Response Time Hours CMTD

terms.name: ⚠️ Average Response Time Hours PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average Response Time in minutes restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD, not the full prior calendar month). Feeds the "previous" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Average Response Time CMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date PMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Minutes to Respond]) — Avg() with Set Analysis, not flag-multiplication, for the same reason as the CMTD version: null Minutes to Respond on unresponded incidents would otherwise deflate the average. FIX (2026-08-10): switched from hour-based date math to the dedicated [Minutes to Respond] field. [Opened Date PMTD] stores text 'Yes'/'No', not 1/0. Synonyms: prior month response time, last month pickup time.

linksTo.subResourceName: INC: Average Response Time Hours PMTD

terms.name: ⚠️ Closed By
terms.description: The person who formally closed this ITIL record after resolution was confirmed. Closure may be performed by the resolver, a service desk agent or automatically by the system after a defined period. Synonyms: closed by, who closed it, closure agent.

terms.name: ⚠️ Escalation Level
terms.description: The current escalation level of this incident. Indicates how far up the management chain the incident has been escalated. Higher escalation levels indicate unresolved high-impact incidents requiring management attention. Escalation Level 0 means no escalation. Escalation Level 1+ means management has been engaged. Use to filter for incidents currently under management scrutiny. Synonyms: escalation, escalated, management escalation, escalation tier.

terms.name: ⚠️ FCR CMTD %
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: First Contact Resolution % for the Current Month To Date window (Opened Date CMTD = Yes). CMTD compares the same day-of-month range as PMTD (e.g. Jul 1-28 vs Jun 1-28), never a partial-month-vs-full-month mismatch, so the two are always a fair trend comparison regardless of where in the month you're looking. This is the "current" reading on the Incident KPI ticker, paired with FCR PMTD % for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [First Contact Resolution] * [Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date CMTD]) — uses the Incident Counter flag-multiplication pattern (SQL-portable) rather than Count()/set analysis. Shares the same First Contact Resolution flag caveat as FCR Rate: currently built as "no reassignment AND no reopen," a routing proxy rather than the strict ITIL repeat-contact definition. Synonyms: current month FCR, this month FCR, FCR trend current.

terms.name: ⚠️ FCR PMTD %
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: First Contact Resolution % for the Prior Month To Date window (Opened Date PMTD = Yes) — the same day-of-month cutoff as the current CMTD window (e.g. Jun 1-28 mirroring Jul 1-28), NOT the full prior calendar month. This is the "previous" reading on the Incident KPI ticker, paired with FCR CMTD % to compute the trend delta/arrow. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [First Contact Resolution] * [Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date PMTD]) — same Incident Counter flag-multiplication pattern as FCR CMTD % for direct SQL portability. Shares the same First Contact Resolution flag caveat as FCR Rate: currently built as "no reassignment AND no reopen," a routing proxy rather than the strict ITIL repeat-contact definition. Synonyms: prior month FCR, last month FCR, FCR trend previous.

terms.name: ⚠️ FCR Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: First Contact Resolution Rate — the percentage of incidents resolved on the caller's first contact without reassignment or follow-up. High FCR indicates effective triage, correct initial routing and strong resolver capability. Expression: Sum([First Contact Resolution]) / Count([Incident ID]). Industry benchmark: elite service desks achieve 70-75%+ FCR. A low FCR combined with high Was Reassigned rate signals a routing or skills gap. Synonyms: FCR rate, first call resolution rate, one-touch rate, resolved first time percentage.

terms.name: ⚠️ First Contact Resolution
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident was resolved on the caller's first contact without reassignment or follow-up. The numerator for FCR Rate = Sum([First Contact Resolution]) / Count([Incident ID]). High FCR indicates effective triage and resolver capability. Source: derived in CONFORM layer from reassignment count and resolution pattern. Synonyms: FCR, first call resolution, one-touch resolution, resolved first time.

terms.name: ⚠️ High Priority
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident is Priority P1 or P2. Used as a fast filter for executive dashboards showing critical and high priority incidents without needing set analysis on the Priority field. Sum([High Priority]) counts all P1+P2 incidents. Synonyms: critical incident, major incident, P1 P2, urgent incident, high severity.

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Open P1 Critical Count
terms.description:
Count of open P1 Critical incidents. Highest severity — requires immediate response. Monitor in real time. Any non-zero P1 count typically triggers a major incident bridge. Synonyms: P1 count, critical incidents, SEV1 open, how many P1s.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}, Priority={'1 - Critical'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Open P2 High Count
terms.description:
Count of open P2 High incidents. Significant impact requiring urgent but not immediate response. A large P2 backlog often signals capacity issues in the resolver teams. Synonyms: P2 count, high incidents, SEV2 open, how many P2s.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}, Priority={'2 - High'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Open P3 Moderate Count
terms.description:
Count of open P3 Moderate incidents. Standard priority — important but not business-stopping. Typically the largest volume bucket. Use to assess overall service desk workload. Synonyms: P3 count, moderate incidents, medium priority open, how many P3s.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}, Priority={'3 - Moderate'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Open P4 Low Count
terms.description:
Count of open P4 Low incidents. Minimal business impact — can be worked opportunistically. A rising P4 backlog may indicate low-priority work being deprioritized indefinitely. Synonyms: P4 count, low priority incidents, how many P4s.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}, Priority={'4 - Low'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Open P5 Planning Count
terms.description:
Count of open P5 Planning priority incidents. Planning-priority records represent work that is logged and tracked but not yet operationally active — they exist in the backlog but have not been assigned urgency or impact. Use to explain the gap between Total Open Incidents and the sum of P1-P4 priority counts. Synonyms: P5 count, planning incidents, backlog incidents, how many P5s.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}, Priority={'5 - Planning'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Status In Progress Count
terms.description:
Count of incidents actively being worked — assigned and in progress by a resolver. The healthy working state. Synonyms: in progress incidents, active work, being worked, how many in progress.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]={'In Progress'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Status New Count
terms.description:
Count of incidents in New status — logged but not yet assigned or in progress. A rising New count indicates intake backlog or assignment delays. Synonyms: new incidents, unassigned incidents, intake backlog, how many new.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]={'New'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Status On Hold Count
terms.description:
Count of incidents paused and waiting on a third party, customer, or scheduled action. A high On Hold count may indicate external dependency bottlenecks or chronic waiting. Synonyms: on hold incidents, waiting incidents, paused incidents, blocked incidents, how many on hold.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]={'On Hold'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Status Resolved Count
terms.description:
Count of incidents in Resolved status — fix applied and pending customer confirmation before formal closure. A large Resolved count that doesn't progress to Closed may indicate a broken closure process. Synonyms: resolved incidents, pending closure, awaiting confirmation, how many resolved.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]={'Resolved'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ INC: Total Open Incidents
terms.description:
Total count of all currently open incidents. Excludes Resolved, Closed, and Canceled. The primary headline KPI for the Incidents dashboard — use as the anchor number for all open incident context. Synonyms: open incidents, active incidents, outstanding incidents, how many open, incident backlog.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Incident'}, [Lifecycle Status]-={'Resolved','Closed','Canceled'}>} [Incident ID])

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident
terms.description: An unplanned interruption to an IT service or a reduction in the quality of an IT service. ITIL 5 defines Incident Management as the practice of minimizing the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible. In the Service Intelligence accelerator, Incident records originate from ServiceNow (incident table) and are identified by Record Type = 'Incident' in the ITIL_Facts table. Key ITIL 5 KPIs: Mean Time To Restore (MTTR), First Contact Resolution (FCR) rate, SLA Compliance rate, Reopen Rate, Reassignment Rate. Conformed date fields: Opened Date (opened_at), Started Date (work_start), Mitigated Date (escalation timestamp), Resolved Date (resolved_at), Closed Date (closed_at). Synonyms: ticket, issue, outage, service disruption, fault.

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident Age Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping incidents by age range for distribution charts. Examples: Same Day, 1-3 Days, 4-7 Days, 8-14 Days, 15-30 Days, Over 30 Days. Use as a chart dimension to show the age distribution of open incidents. Synonyms: age bucket, age group, age range, age category.

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident Age Days
terms.description: The number of days this incident has been open since Opened Date. For resolved incidents this is the total lifespan. For open incidents this is the current age. Use with Incident Age Band for distribution analysis. Expression: Today() - Floor([Opened Date]). Source field: Derived in CONFORM layer. Synonyms: age, days open, how old, incident age, open duration.

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident ID
terms.description: Unique sys_id identifier for the Incident record. Use Count([Incident ID]) as the base count expression for all incident KPIs. Never use Count(*) — Incident ID ensures correct counting in the conformed ITIL_Facts table where Problems and Changes also exist. Source field: Incident = sys_id (INC rows only). Synonyms: incident sys_id, INC sys_id, record ID.

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident Number
terms.description: Human-readable incident number (e.g. INC0012345). Use as the display identifier in drill-through tables. Use Incident ID for joins and counting. Source field: Incident = number. Synonyms: INC number, ticket number, incident reference, case number.

terms.name: ⚠️ Incident URL
terms.description: Clickable URL linking directly to the incident record in ServiceNow. Use in drill-through tables so analysts can jump from the dashboard to the live ticket with one click. Built in CONFORM layer as [ServiceNow Base URL]/incident.do?sys_id=[Incident ID]. Synonyms: incident link, INC URL, ServiceNow link, open ticket.

terms.name: ⚠️ Is Active
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident is currently open and unresolved. Is Active = Yes means the incident is still impacting users right now. Used in open incident KPIs: Sum([Is Active]) = total open incident count. Is Active = No means the incident has been resolved or closed. Synonyms: open, unresolved, active, still open, current, outstanding, in progress.

terms.name: ⚠️ Knowledge Created
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when a knowledge article was created as a result of resolving this incident. Knowledge creation is an ITIL 5 best practice — high knowledge creation rates indicate a learning organization that prevents repeat incidents. Sum([Knowledge Created]) counts incidents that generated reusable knowledge. Synonyms: KB article created, knowledge base, article created, documented solution.

terms.name: ⚠️ Lifecycle Status Code
terms.description: The raw numeric state code from ServiceNow before conformation to Lifecycle Status labels. Values: 1=New, 2=In Progress, 3=On Hold, 6=Resolved, 7=Closed, 8=Canceled. Use Lifecycle Status for display and filtering — use Lifecycle Status Code only when you need to filter by the raw numeric value or when troubleshooting state mapping issues. Synonyms: state code, numeric state, raw state, incident state code.

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Mean Time To Restore — the average time elapsed from when an incident was opened to when it was resolved. The primary ITIL 5 Incident Management KPI and one of the four DORA elite performance metrics. Calculated as the average difference between Resolved Date and Opened Date. Three variants available: MTTR Business Hours (excludes nights and weekends), MTTR Business Days, MTTR Calendar Hours (raw elapsed time). Lower MTTR indicates faster service restoration. Industry benchmarks vary by priority: P1 targets typically under 4 business hours, P5 targets may be days. Expression: Avg([MTTR Business Hours]). Synonyms: mean time to restore, mean time to recover, average resolution time, average fix time, how long to fix, time to resolve.

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR Business Days
terms.description: MTTR measured in business days. Useful for executive reporting where day-level granularity is sufficient. Expression: Avg([MTTR Business Days]). Synonyms: business days MTTR, days to resolve, working days resolution.

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR Business Hours
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Mean Time To Resolution in business hours, across all resolved Incidents, lifetime/no date restriction. Denominator restricted to closed incidents via the stored Is NotActive flag (added 2026-07-30 to replace inline (1-Is Active) math for performance). Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [MTTR Business Hours]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Is NotActive]). Verified: Is NotActive is an exact inverse of Is Active across all rows, no mismatches. Synonyms: MTTR, mean time to resolve, average resolution time, business hours MTTR.

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR Business Hours CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: MTTR Business Hours restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. Uses stored Is NotActive flag instead of inline (1-Is Active) math. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [MTTR Business Hours] * [Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Is NotActive] * [Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR Business Hours PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: MTTR Business Hours restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. Uses stored Is NotActive flag. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [MTTR Business Hours] * [Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Is NotActive] * [Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: ⚠️ MTTR Calendar Hours
terms.description: MTTR measured in calendar hours including nights and weekends. Useful for 24x7 operations where resolution is expected around the clock regardless of business hours. Typically larger than MTTR Business Hours for incidents spanning weekends. Synonyms: calendar hours MTTR, total elapsed hours, wall clock hours, 24x7 MTTR.

terms.name: ⚠️ Major Incident
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident has been formally declared a Major Incident requiring executive involvement and a post-incident review. Major Incidents typically represent P1 events with widespread business impact. Sum([Major Incident]) counts all major incidents. Synonyms: P1 major, major outage, Sev 1, severity 1, critical event.

terms.name: ⚠️ Major Incident Count CMTD
terms.description: OPERATIONAL KPI: Count of incidents formally declared a Major Incident, restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month, day-of-month aligned to PMTD for a fair trend comparison). Feeds the "current" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Major Incident Count PMTD. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [Major Incident] * [Opened Date CMTD]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): Major Incident is currently "No" for all 95 incidents in this dataset - none have ever been declared, so this will show a flat 0 until major-incident scenarios are backfilled. Synonyms: current month major incident count, this month P1 major count.

terms.name: ⚠️ Major Incident Count PMTD
terms.description: OPERATIONAL KPI: Count of incidents formally declared a Major Incident, restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD, not the full prior calendar month). Feeds the "previous" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Major Incident Count CMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [Major Incident] * [Opened Date PMTD]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): Major Incident is currently "No" for all 95 incidents in this dataset - none have ever been declared, so this will show a flat 0 until major-incident scenarios are backfilled. Synonyms: prior month major incident count, last month P1 major count.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date CMTD
terms.description: Current Month To Date period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes from 1st of current month through today. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date CYTD
terms.description: Current Year To Date period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — January 1st through today. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date MRCM
terms.description: Most Recent Complete Month period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — last fully completed calendar month. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Month
terms.description: Calendar month derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — Jan-Dec, sorts 1-12. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date PMTD
terms.description: Prior Month To Date period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — same elapsed day range in prior month as CMTD. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date PRCM
terms.description: Prior Recent Complete Month period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — month immediately before MRCM. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date PYTD
terms.description: Prior Year To Date period flag derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — same elapsed portion of prior year as CYTD. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Quarter
terms.description: Calendar quarter number derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Values 1-4. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Week
terms.description: ISO week number derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Values 1-52. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Weekday
terms.description: Day of week derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — Mon-Sun, sorts by day number. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Year
terms.description: Calendar year derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() integer field. Mitigated Date is Incident-only — null for Problems and Changes. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Year Month
terms.description: Year and month combined derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — YYYY-MMM, sorts chronologically. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Mitigated Date Year Quarter
terms.description: Year and quarter combined derived from Mitigated Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — YYYY-Q#, sorts chronologically. Incident-only. Source field: Incident = upon_approval.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reassignment Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping incidents by number of reassignments. Examples: No Reassignments, 1 Reassignment, 2-3 Reassignments, 4+ Reassignments. Use to identify the proportion of incidents that bounce excessively between teams. High reassignment bands signal routing problems. Synonyms: reassignment bucket, bounce band, transfer band.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reassignment Count
terms.description: The total number of times this incident was reassigned to a different team or individual. High Reassignment Count indicates incorrect initial routing. Use Avg([Reassignment Count]) to track routing quality. The Was Reassigned flag is the binary version — use Reassignment Count when the exact number matters. Synonyms: number of reassignments, bounce count, transfer count, how many times reassigned.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reassignment Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The percentage of incidents that were reassigned to a different team or individual after initial assignment. High reassignment rates increase MTTR, reduce FCR and indicate incorrect initial routing or skill gaps. Expression: Sum([Was Reassigned]) / Count([Incident ID]). Targets vary but under 10% is typical. Break down by Fulfillment Team to identify which teams are most frequently reassigning work. Synonyms: reassignment rate, bounce rate, transfer rate, wrong team rate, reroute rate.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reopen Count
terms.description: The total number of times this incident record has been reopened after resolution. Reopen Count > 1 indicates a persistently difficult-to-resolve incident. Use Avg([Reopen Count]) to track resolution quality trends. The Was Reopened flag is the binary version — use Reopen Count when the exact number of reopens matters. Synonyms: number of reopens, reopen frequency, how many times reopened.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reopen Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The percentage of incidents that were reopened after being marked resolved. High reopen rates indicate resolution quality problems — the fix didn't hold or the root cause wasn't addressed. Expression: Sum([Was Reopened]) / Count([Incident ID]). A healthy service desk targets under 5% reopen rate. High reopen rates often correlate with low FCR Rate and high Was Reassigned rates. Synonyms: reopen rate, reopened percentage, resolution failure rate, came back rate.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reopened % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Reopened Incidents % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month, day-of-month aligned to PMTD for a fair trend comparison). Feeds the "current" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Reopened % PMTD. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [Was Reopened] * [Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date CMTD]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): Was Reopened is currently "No" for all 95 incidents in this dataset - zero reopens have ever occurred, so this will show a flat 0.0% until reopen scenarios are backfilled. Synonyms: current month reopen rate, this month reopened percentage.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reopened % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Reopened Incidents % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD, not the full prior calendar month). Feeds the "previous" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with Reopened % CMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [Was Reopened] * [Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date PMTD]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): Was Reopened is currently "No" for all 95 incidents in this dataset - zero reopens have ever occurred, so this will show a flat 0.0% until reopen scenarios are backfilled. Synonyms: prior month reopen rate, last month reopened percentage.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reported By
terms.description: The user who reported this incident to the service desk. Use to analyze which users or departments generate the most requests. Source field: Incident = caller_id. Synonyms: caller, submitted by, raised by, end user, affected user.

terms.name: ⚠️ Reporting Channel
terms.description: The channel through which this ITIL record was submitted. Identifies how the record entered the system — Self Service Portal, Phone, Email, Chat, Monitoring Alert, API/Automation. Used to analyze channel distribution, self-service adoption rates and automation coverage. Primarily populated for Incidents. Synonyms: submission channel, intake channel, how reported, how submitted, entry channel, contact channel.

terms.name: ⚠️ Resolution Time Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping incidents by resolution time range for distribution analysis. Examples: Under 1 Hour, 1-4 Hours, 4-8 Hours, 1-3 Days, Over 3 Days. Use alongside MTTR to understand the distribution of resolution times not just the average. Synonyms: resolution time bucket, resolution band, how long to fix band.

terms.name: ⚠️ SLA Compliance % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: SLA Compliance % for the Current Month To Date window (Opened Date CMTD = Yes), day-of-month aligned to PMTD for a fair trend comparison. Feeds the "current" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with SLA Compliance % PMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [SLA Met] * [Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date CMTD]) - Incident Counter flag-multiplication pattern, SQL-portable. CAVEAT (2026-07-29): sla_due is currently NULL on every incident in this ServiceNow instance - no SLA Definition is attached to the incident flow, so this will show 100% until real SLA target dates exist. Do not present as an earned result until that data gap is fixed. Synonyms: current month SLA rate, this month SLA compliance.

terms.name: ⚠️ SLA Compliance % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: SLA Compliance % for the Prior Month To Date window (Opened Date PMTD = Yes) - same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD, not the full prior calendar month. Feeds the "previous" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with SLA Compliance % CMTD to compute the trend delta. Expression: Sum([Incident Counter] * [SLA Met] * [Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Incident Counter] * [Opened Date PMTD]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): sla_due is currently NULL on every incident in this ServiceNow instance - no SLA Definition is attached to the incident flow, so this will show 100% until real SLA target dates exist. Do not present as an earned result until that data gap is fixed. Synonyms: prior month SLA rate, last month SLA compliance.

terms.name: ⚠️ SLA Compliance Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The percentage of incidents resolved within their contracted SLA target time. The primary SLA governance metric. Expression: Sum([SLA Met]) / Count([Incident ID]). A declining SLA compliance rate is the primary signal of service degradation and should trigger immediate investigation. Target thresholds are organization-defined but 95%+ is typical for enterprise IT. Breaking down SLA Compliance Rate by Priority reveals whether P1/P2 targets are being missed disproportionately. Synonyms: SLA compliance, SLA hit rate, within SLA percentage, on-time resolution rate, SLA performance.

terms.name: ⚠️ SLA Met
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident was resolved within its contracted SLA target time. The numerator for SLA Compliance Rate = Sum([SLA Met]) / Count([Incident ID]). A declining SLA Met rate is the primary indicator of service degradation. Source: derived from SLA Target Date vs Resolved Date comparison in CONFORM layer. Synonyms: SLA compliance, within SLA, SLA hit, on time, met target.

terms.name: ⚠️ Same Day Resolution
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident was resolved on the same calendar day it was opened. A strong positive signal for service desk responsiveness. Same Day Resolution Rate = Sum([Same Day Resolution]) / Count([Incident ID]). Synonyms: resolved same day, day-of resolution, quick resolution, same day fix.

terms.name: ⚠️ Severity
terms.description: The severity classification of an incident independent of priority. Where Priority combines impact and urgency into a single P1-P5 scale, Severity focuses on the technical impact magnitude. Not all organizations use both Priority and Severity — in some implementations Severity is synonymous with Priority. Synonyms: severity level, technical severity, impact severity.

terms.name: ⚠️ Was Reassigned
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident was reassigned to a different team or individual after initial assignment. Reassignment indicates incorrect initial routing or skill gaps. Reassignment Rate = Sum([Was Reassigned]) / Count([Incident ID]). High reassignment rates increase MTTR and reduce FCR. Synonyms: bounced, rerouted, transferred, reassigned, wrong team.

terms.name: ⚠️ Was Reopened
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when the incident was reopened after being marked resolved. Reopened incidents indicate resolution quality issues — the fix didn't hold or the root cause wasn't addressed. Reopen Rate = Sum([Was Reopened]) / Count([Incident ID]). High reopen rates often correlate with low FCR. Synonyms: reopened, came back, re-escalated, resolution failed.

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Days to Known Error
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The average number of days from when a problem was opened to when it was confirmed as a Known Error. Measures problem investigation velocity. Expression: Avg([Days to Known Error]). A low Days to Known Error indicates a proactive problem management practice that quickly identifies root causes. Break down by Priority to ensure major problems receive fastest investigation. Synonyms: days to known error, time to known error, known error identification time, root cause time.

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Days to Resolution (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average time in days to permanent resolution, lifetime/no date restriction. FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis instead of flag-multiplication, same fix as Change Lead Time/Implementation Duration - a (1-Is Active) denominator carries the same asymmetry risk once this field's true population pattern is known. Expression: Avg([Days to Resolution]). CAVEAT: Days to Resolution is confirmed EMPTY across the entire dataset right now - this will return null until the source field is populated in the conform layer. Not a formula bug.
