Synonyms: time to resolution, average problem resolution time, days to permanent fix.

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Days to Resolution CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Days to Resolution restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date CMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Days to Resolution]). CAVEAT: Days to Resolution is confirmed EMPTY across the entire dataset - will return null until populated in the conform layer.

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Days to Resolution PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Avg Days to Resolution restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). FIX (2026-07-30): rebuilt using Avg() with set analysis. Expression: Avg({<[Opened Date PMTD]={'Yes'}>} [Days to Resolution]). CAVEAT: same confirmed-EMPTY field as the Lifetime and CMTD versions.

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Avg Days to Resolution PMTD

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Hours to Known Error (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average hours from problem opened_at to confirmed known error status, across all Problems that have reached Known Error. Measures root cause identification speed — lower is better. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Hours to Known Error]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]). NOTE: field renamed from [Days to Known Error] to [Hours to Known Error] in conform layer (value = days × 24). Numerator must include [Known Error] flag or non-KE records inflate the average. Synonyms: time to known error, RCA speed, root cause investigation time.

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Avg Days to Known Error (Lifetime)

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Hours to Known Error CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average hours from opened_at to known error confirmation, restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month), among Problems that reached Known Error. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Hours to Known Error]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Opened Date CMTD]). NOTE: field renamed from [Days to Known Error] to [Hours to Known Error]; numerator includes [Known Error] flag.

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Avg Days to Known Error CMTD

terms.name: 🔍 Avg Hours to Known Error PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Average hours from opened_at to known error confirmation, restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month), among Problems that reached Known Error. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Hours to Known Error]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Opened Date PMTD]). NOTE: field renamed from [Days to Known Error] to [Hours to Known Error]; numerator includes [Known Error] flag.

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Avg Days to Known Error PMTD

terms.name: 🔍 Days to Known Error
terms.description: The number of days from when this problem was opened to when it was confirmed as a Known Error. Measures how quickly the investigation team identifies and documents the root cause. Lower values indicate a more effective problem management practice. Avg([Days to Known Error]) is the KPI expression. Null for problems not yet confirmed as Known Errors. Synonyms: time to known error, days to identify root cause, investigation duration, how long to find root cause.

terms.name: 🔍 Duplicate Of ID
terms.description: The sys_id of another problem record that this problem is a duplicate of. When populated indicates this problem investigation was merged into the referenced problem. Useful for deduplication analysis. Synonyms: duplicate problem, parent problem, merged into.

terms.name: 🔍 Has Linked Change % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Problems with a Linked Change raised to implement the fix, across all active Problems, lifetime/no date restriction. Shows how often root-cause analysis actually results in a formal remediation Change rather than staying a documentation-only fix. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Has Linked Change]) / Sum([Problem Counter]). Synonyms: linked change rate, RCA to remediation rate, problem-to-change conversion %.

terms.name: 🔍 Has Linked Change % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Has Linked Change % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Has Linked Change]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Has Linked Change % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Has Linked Change % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Has Linked Change]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Has Permanent Fix
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when a permanent fix has been implemented and confirmed for this problem. Has Permanent Fix = Yes means the problem is fully resolved and should not generate further incidents. Sum([Has Permanent Fix]) / Count([Problem ID]) shows the permanent fix rate. Synonyms: permanently fixed, root cause resolved, permanent resolution, definitive fix implemented.

terms.name: 🔍 Investigation Team
terms.description: The specific team assigned to investigate this Problem record in ServiceNow. Problem-specific equivalent of Fulfillment Team. In the ITIL_Facts table this field is populated only for Problem rows — null for Incidents and Changes. Source field: ServiceNow problem table assignment_group. Synonyms: problem team, root cause team, investigation group, who is investigating.

terms.name: 🔍 Known Error
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this problem has been confirmed as a Known Error — meaning the root cause is understood and documented even if a permanent fix is not yet available. Known Error Rate = Sum([Known Error]) / Count([Problem ID]). A high Known Error rate indicates a mature problem management practice. Known Errors with workarounds prevent repeat incidents. Synonyms: known error, KEDB, root cause known, confirmed error, documented error.

terms.name: 🔍 Known Error Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The percentage of problems that have been confirmed as Known Errors. Indicates problem management maturity — a high Known Error rate means the team is identifying and documenting root causes effectively. Expression: Sum([Known Error]) / Count([Problem ID]). Known Errors with workarounds prevent repeat incidents from consuming service desk capacity. Synonyms: known error rate, KEDB coverage, root cause documentation rate, known error percentage.

terms.name: 🔍 Known Error Rate % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Problems where root cause has been confirmed as a Known Error, across all active Problems, lifetime/no date restriction. The primary root-cause-analysis progress metric. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Known Error]) / Sum([Problem Counter]). Synonyms: known error rate, root cause identified %, RCA completion rate.

terms.name: 🔍 Known Error Rate % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Known Error Rate % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with Known Error Rate % PMTD. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Known Error Rate % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Known Error Rate % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot, paired with Known Error Rate % CMTD for the trend arrow. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Known Error]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Major Problem
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this problem has been formally classified as a Major Problem requiring senior management attention and a dedicated post-problem review. Major Problems typically originate from Major Incidents. Synonyms: major problem, critical problem, high priority problem, P1 problem.

terms.name: 🔍 Major Problem % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Problems formally classified as Major Problem (senior management attention, dedicated post-problem review), across all active Problems, lifetime/no date restriction. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Major Problem]) / Sum([Problem Counter]). CAVEAT (2026-07-29): currently a flat 0% across all 32 Problems in this dataset - same pattern as Major Incident Count, not yet verified whether the flag is genuinely never true here or blocked by a read-only field similar to major_incident_state on the Incident table. Synonyms: major problem rate, critical problem %, senior escalation rate.

terms.name: 🔍 Major Problem % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Major Problem % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Major Problem]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]). CAVEAT: flat 0% in the Lifetime version too - same pattern as Major Incident Count, not yet verified whether genuinely never true or blocked by a read-only field.

terms.name: 🔍 Major Problem % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Major Problem % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Major Problem]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Known Error Count
terms.description:
Count of open problems confirmed as Known Errors — defects with documented workarounds awaiting permanent fix. A key ITIL metric: known errors should have workarounds and a fix plan. Synonyms: known errors, how many known errors, confirmed defects.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]-={'Resolved','Closed'}, [Known Error]={'Yes'}>} [Problem ID])

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Status Assess Count
terms.description:
Count of problems in Assess status — actively being investigated to determine root cause. Maps to 'In Analysis' in the Root Cause Status panel. Synonyms: in analysis, being assessed, under investigation.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]={'Assess'}>} [Problem ID])

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Status Fix In Progress Count
terms.description:
Count of problems in Fix in Progress status — root cause identified, permanent fix being implemented. Synonyms: fix being applied, remediation in progress, how many being fixed.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]={'Fix in Progress'}>} [Problem ID])

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Status Fix In Progress Count

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Status New Count
terms.description:
Count of problems in New status — logged but investigation not yet started. Maps to 'Pending' in the Root Cause Status panel. Synonyms: pending problems, unassigned problems, new problems.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]={'New'}>} [Problem ID])

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Status Root Cause Analysis Count
terms.description:
Count of problems in Root Cause Analysis status — the root cause is being formally documented. Maps to 'Identified' in the Root Cause Status panel. Synonyms: RCA status, root cause identified, how many in RCA.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]={'Root Cause Analysis'}>} [Problem ID])

linksTo.subResourceName: PRB: Status Root Cause Analysis Count

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Total Open Problems
terms.description:
Total count of all open problems — excludes Resolved and Closed. Primary headline KPI for the Problems dashboard. Synonyms: open problems, active problems, problem backlog, how many problems.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]-={'Resolved','Closed'}>} [Problem ID])

terms.name: 🔍 PRB: Workaround Available Count
terms.description:
Count of open problems that have a documented workaround available. Users can be redirected to the workaround while the permanent fix is in progress. Synonyms: workaround available, has workaround, how many have workarounds.

Expression: Count({<[Record Type]={'Problem'}, [Problem Status]-={'Resolved','Closed'}, [Workaround Available]={'Yes'}>} [Problem ID])

terms.name: 🔍 Permanent Fix Description
terms.description: Description of the permanent fix implemented to resolve this problem permanently. Populated when Has Permanent Fix = Yes. Documents what was done to eliminate the root cause so the problem does not recur. Synonyms: permanent fix, definitive fix, how was it permanently fixed, resolution description.

terms.name: 🔍 Permanent Fix Rate % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Problems that have a documented Permanent Fix on file, across all active Problems, lifetime/no date restriction. FIX (2026-07-30): dropped the (1-Is Active) denominator restriction - testing showed 4 of 8 Problems with a real Permanent Fix are still marked active (Has Permanent Fix and Is Active are independent facts about a Problem, not sequential milestones), so restricting to closed-only was excluding half the true population. Now matches the same simple style as Known Error Rate / Workaround Availability. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Has Permanent Fix]) / Sum([Problem Counter]). Synonyms: permanent fix rate, closed the loop %, root cause remediation rate.

terms.name: 🔍 Permanent Fix Rate % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Permanent Fix Rate % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Feeds "current" slot, paired with PMTD. FIX (2026-07-30): dropped the (1-Is Active) denominator restriction - Has Permanent Fix and Is Active are independent facts, not sequential milestones; half of true fixes were being excluded. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Has Permanent Fix] * [Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter] * [Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Permanent Fix Rate % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Permanent Fix Rate % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Feeds "previous" slot for the trend arrow. FIX (2026-07-30): dropped the (1-Is Active) denominator restriction, same fix as Lifetime and CMTD. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Has Permanent Fix] * [Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter] * [Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Problem
terms.description: A cause or potential cause of one or more incidents. ITIL 5 defines Problem Management as the practice of reducing the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes and managing workarounds and known errors. A Problem investigation is triggered when multiple incidents share a common root cause. In the Service Intelligence accelerator, Problem records originate from ServiceNow (problem table) and are identified by Record Type = 'Problem' in the ITIL_Facts table. Key ITIL 5 KPIs: Days to Known Error, Days to Resolution, Known Error rate, Workaround Coverage rate. Conformed date fields: Opened Date (opened_at), Started Date (confirmed_at), Mitigated Date (workaround_communicated_at), Resolved Date (resolved_at), Closed Date (closed_at). Synonyms: root cause, underlying issue, recurring incident, systemic failure.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Age Band
terms.description: A text bucket grouping problems by age range for distribution analysis. Examples: Under 7 Days, 7-30 Days, 30-90 Days, Over 90 Days. Use to identify stalled long-running investigations that need management attention. Synonyms: problem age bucket, investigation age band, age range, how old band.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Age Days
terms.description: The number of days this problem has been open since Opened Date. For resolved problems this is the total investigation lifespan. For open problems this is the current age. High values on open problems indicate stalled investigations. Use with Problem Age Band for distribution analysis. Synonyms: problem age, days open, investigation age, how old.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Category
terms.description: The top-level classification category for this problem. Problem Category groups problems by technology domain or service area (e.g. Network, Applications, Hardware, Security). Use to analyze which categories generate the most recurring problems and target systemic improvement efforts. Synonyms: problem type, problem domain, problem area, category.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem ID
terms.description: Unique sys_id identifier for the Problem record. Use Count([Problem ID]) as the base count expression for all problem KPIs. Source field: Problem = sys_id (PRB rows only). Synonyms: problem sys_id, PRB sys_id, record ID.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Investigator
terms.description: The individual assigned to investigate this problem and identify root cause. Use for individual workload and accountability analysis. Source field: Problem = assigned_to. Synonyms: problem owner, investigator, root cause analyst, who is investigating, problem assignee.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Number
terms.description: Human-readable problem number (e.g. PRB0001234). Use as the display identifier in drill-through tables. Source field: Problem = number. Synonyms: PRB number, problem reference, problem ticket number.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Status
terms.description: The current lifecycle state of a Problem record in ServiceNow. Values: New, Assess, Root Cause Analysis, Fix in Progress, Resolved, Closed. Problem Status is more granular than Lifecycle Status for problem management reporting — use Problem Status when analyzing where problems are stuck in the investigation pipeline. A large count of problems stuck in Root Cause Analysis indicates investigation bottlenecks. Synonyms: problem state, investigation status, where is the problem, problem lifecycle.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Status Code
terms.description: The raw numeric state code for the Problem record from ServiceNow before conformation to Problem Status labels. Use Problem Status for display and filtering — use Problem Status Code only when troubleshooting state mapping or filtering by raw numeric value. Synonyms: problem state code, numeric problem state, raw problem status.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Subcategory
terms.description: The second-level classification beneath Problem Category providing more specific problem grouping. Example: Problem Category = Applications, Problem Subcategory = ERP, or Database, or API. Use together with Problem Category for drill-down analysis of problem distribution. Synonyms: problem sub-type, problem subarea, subcategory.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem Summary
terms.description: A one-line summary describing the problem being investigated. Primary display label for problems in list views. Source for Qlik Answers semantic search — natural language questions about what problems exist will match against Problem Summary content. Synonyms: problem title, problem description, what is the problem, problem name.

terms.name: 🔍 Problem URL
terms.description: Clickable URL linking directly to the problem record in ServiceNow. Built in CONFORM layer as [ServiceNow Base URL]/problem.do?sys_id=[Problem ID]. Synonyms: problem link, PRB URL, ServiceNow link, open problem.

terms.name: 🔍 Related Incident Count
terms.description: The number of incidents currently linked to this problem record in ServiceNow. High Related Incident Count indicates the problem is causing widespread impact across the user community and should be prioritized for resolution. A problem with many related incidents is a strong signal for major problem classification. Synonyms: incident count, how many incidents, linked incidents, associated incidents, affected incidents.

terms.name: 🔍 Root Cause Analysis
terms.description: The full documented root cause of this problem. Populated when the investigation has identified the underlying cause. Root Cause Analysis is the definitive explanation of why the problem occurred. Rich content for Qlik Answers — analysts can ask why a problem happened and get the documented root cause. Synonyms: root cause, why it happened, cause analysis, underlying cause, RCA.

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Availability % (Lifetime)
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of active Problems with a documented workaround available for users while the permanent fix is developed, lifetime/no date restriction. Expression: Sum([Problem Counter] * [Workaround Available]) / Sum([Problem Counter]). Synonyms: workaround availability rate, workaround coverage %, interim fix rate.

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Availability % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Workaround Availability % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Workaround Available]*[Opened Date CMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date CMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Availability % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: Workaround Availability % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD). Expression: Sum([Problem Counter]*[Workaround Available]*[Opened Date PMTD]) / Sum([Problem Counter]*[Opened Date PMTD]).

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Available
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when a workaround has been identified and communicated for this problem. A workaround is a temporary solution that reduces the impact of incidents caused by this problem while a permanent fix is developed. Workaround Coverage = Sum([Workaround Available]) / Count([Problem ID]). Synonyms: workaround exists, workaround documented, temporary fix available, interim fix.

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Coverage Rate
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: The percentage of problems for which a workaround has been identified and communicated. Workaround coverage reduces the impact of known problems on end users while permanent fixes are developed. Expression: Sum([Workaround Available]) / Count([Problem ID]). High workaround coverage combined with low permanent fix rate may indicate a backlog of deferred permanent fixes. Synonyms: workaround coverage, workaround availability, interim fix rate, temporary fix coverage.

terms.name: 🔍 Workaround Instructions
terms.description: Step-by-step instructions for applying the workaround for this problem. End users and service desk agents use this to reduce incident impact while the permanent fix is in development. Rich Qlik Answers content — asking how to work around a known problem should surface this field. Synonyms: workaround steps, how to work around it, interim fix instructions, temporary solution.

terms.name: 🤖 AI Resolution Suggestion
terms.description: An AI-generated suggested resolution for this incident based on analysis of the incident description and historical resolution patterns. Populated by AI processing in the CONFORM layer. Use as a Qlik Answers knowledge source — when an analyst asks 'how was this type of incident typically resolved?' the AI Resolution Suggestion field contains the contextual answer. Null for incidents processed before AI enrichment was enabled. Synonyms: AI suggestion, suggested fix, recommended resolution, AI recommendation, automated resolution hint.

terms.name: 🤖 AI Sentiment Score
terms.description: An AI-generated sentiment score for this incident derived from analysis of the incident description, notes and resolution text. Indicates the emotional tone of the interaction — positive sentiment suggests a smooth resolution experience, negative sentiment may indicate user frustration or difficult resolution process. Use to identify patterns in poorly-rated interactions and prioritize service improvement efforts. Synonyms: sentiment, user sentiment, interaction sentiment, experience score, NLP score.

terms.name: 🤖 AI-Assisted Resolution %
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: % of Incidents where ServiceNow's AI Agent (Platform AI Agents and Skills scope) generated a resolution plan for a human resolver to follow, lifetime/no date restriction. Sourced from ai_resolution_plan on the task table, surfaced in Qlik as AI Resolution Assistance. DEFINITION NOTE: this is AI-ASSISTED resolution, not autonomous auto-resolution - a populated plan means AI drafted a suggestion, not that the incident closed with zero human involvement. Related but distinct from AI Resolution Suggestion (a separate, currently unpopulated field). Expression: Num(SUM(incident_counter * ai_resolution_assistance)/SUM(incident_counter),'0.0%'). Synonyms: AI assist rate, AI plan rate, AI-drafted resolution %.

terms.name: 🤖 AI-Assisted Resolution % CMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: AI-Assisted Resolution % restricted to Opened Date CMTD = Yes (current month, day-of-month aligned to PMTD for a fair equal-length trend comparison). Feeds the "current" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with AI-Assisted Resolution % PMTD for the delta arrow. DEFINITION NOTE: AI-ASSISTED, not auto-resolved - see AI-Assisted Resolution % for the full caveat. Expression: Num(SUM(incident_counter * ai_resolution_assistance * opened_date_cmtd)/SUM(incident_counter * opened_date_cmtd),'0.0%'). Synonyms: current month AI assist rate, this month AI plan rate.

terms.name: 🤖 AI-Assisted Resolution % PMTD
terms.description: PERFORMANCE KPI: AI-Assisted Resolution % restricted to Opened Date PMTD = Yes (prior month, same day-of-month cutoff as CMTD, not the full prior calendar month). Feeds the "previous" slot of the Incident KPI ticker, paired with AI-Assisted Resolution % CMTD for the trend arrow. DEFINITION NOTE: AI-ASSISTED, not auto-resolved - see AI-Assisted Resolution % for the full caveat. Expression: Num(SUM(incident_counter * ai_resolution_assistance * opened_date_pmtd)/SUM(incident_counter * opened_date_pmtd),'0.0%'). Synonyms: prior month AI assist rate, last month AI plan rate.

terms.name: 🧩 Affected Service
terms.description: The service or application affected by this ITIL record. Primary dimension for service-level analysis across all three practice areas. Use to identify which services generate the most incidents, problems or changes. Source field by record type: Incident = u_business_service, Problem = u_business_service, Change = u_business_service. Synonyms: service, application, affected application, impacted service, which service.

terms.name: 🧩 Business Impact
terms.description: The assessed business impact of this ITIL record. Combined with Resolution Urgency to derive Priority. Indicates how broadly the issue affects the organization. Source field by record type: Incident = impact, Problem = impact, Change = impact. Synonyms: impact, business impact level, how many users affected, scope of impact.

terms.name: 🧩 CMTD
terms.description: CALENDAR INTELLIGENCE: Current Month To Date — a Dual(Yes/No) period flag that is Yes for all dates from the first day of the current calendar month through today. Used to filter any conformed date field to the current month's activity in progress. Example: selecting Opened Date CMTD = Yes shows all records opened so far this month. Because CMTD is a Dual field, Sum([Opened Date CMTD]) counts records opened this month without set analysis. Available on all five conformed date fields: Opened Date CMTD, Started Date CMTD, Mitigated Date CMTD, Resolved Date CMTD, Closed Date CMTD. Synonyms: current month, this month, MTD, month to date, current MTD.

terms.name: 🧩 CONFORM Layer
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The second layer of the ITIL 5 Accelerator pipeline. Reads RAW QVDs and applies ITIL 5 field conformance — translating native source system field names into ITIL 5 standard terminology, applying performance flags, joining the MasterCalendar for date intelligence, adding URL links and writing COMMENT FIELD governance metadata. Work done once in the CONFORM layer is inherited by every downstream visualization application. Applications in this layer: Conform Data. Output: Conform_Incidents.qvd, Conform_Problems.qvd, Conform_Changes.qvd, Conform_Master_Calendar.qvd. Synonyms: conform layer, conformed data, silver layer, transformation layer, governance layer.

terms.name: 🧩 CYTD
terms.description: CALENDAR INTELLIGENCE: Current Year To Date — a Dual(Yes/No) period flag that is Yes for all dates from January 1st of the current calendar year through today. Used to analyze full year performance in progress. Example: Opened Date CYTD = Yes shows all records opened so far this year. Compare CYTD vs PYTD for year-over-year trending on the same elapsed portion of the year. Available on all five conformed date fields. Synonyms: current year, this year, year to date, YTD, current YTD.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date
terms.description: CONFORMED DATE: The date and time the ITIL record was formally completed and signed off. Represents the final administrative closure of the record after resolution has been confirmed. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at (ServiceNow incident table), Change = closed_at (ServiceNow change_request table), Problem = closed_at (ServiceNow problem table). NOTE: Closed Date differs from Resolved Date — a record is resolved when the work is done but closed when it is formally signed off, which may happen immediately or days later. For Incidents specifically a user asking 'how many incidents did we close last month' may mean either Resolved Date or Closed Date depending on their organization's process — check which date aligns with their SLA reporting before choosing. Synonyms: closure date, closed date, sign off date, formally closed, when closed, completion date, final date, closed_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date CMTD
terms.description: Current Month To Date period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes from 1st of current month through today. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date CYTD
terms.description: Current Year To Date period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — January 1st through today. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date MRCM
terms.description: Most Recent Complete Month period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — last fully completed calendar month. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Month
terms.description: Calendar month derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — Jan-Dec, sorts 1-12. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date PMTD
terms.description: Prior Month To Date period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — same elapsed day range in prior month as CMTD. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date PRCM
terms.description: Prior Recent Complete Month period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — month immediately before MRCM. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date PYTD
terms.description: Prior Year To Date period flag derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — same elapsed portion of prior year as CYTD. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Quarter
terms.description: Calendar quarter number derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Values 1-4. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Week
terms.description: ISO week number derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Values 1-52. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Weekday
terms.description: Day of week derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — Mon-Sun, sorts by day number. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Year
terms.description: Calendar year derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() integer field. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Year Month
terms.description: Year and month combined derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — YYYY-MMM, sorts chronologically. Primary trend axis for monthly closure charts. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Closed Date Year Quarter
terms.description: Year and quarter combined derived from Closed Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() — YYYY-Q#, sorts chronologically. Source field by record type: Incident = closed_at, Problem = closed_at, Change = close_date.

terms.name: 🧩 Configuration Item
terms.description: The specific configuration item (server, application, device) involved in this ITIL record. More granular than Affected Service. Use to identify which CIs generate the most incidents, require the most changes, or are linked to the most problems. Source field by record type: Incident = cmdb_ci, Problem = cmdb_ci, Change = cmdb_ci. Synonyms: CI, asset, configuration item, server, device, which CI.

terms.name: 🧩 Created Date
terms.description: System timestamp when this ITIL record was created in ServiceNow. Distinct from Opened Date which may be backdated. Use for audit trail and data freshness monitoring. The MAX Created Date in the dataset indicates the most recent record the pipeline has loaded. Source field by record type: Incident = sys_created_on, Problem = sys_created_on, Change = sys_created_on. Synonyms: creation date, when created, system created date, record created.

terms.name: 🧩 First Reported Incident
terms.description: The Incident ID of the first incident that triggered this problem investigation. Provides traceability from the problem back to its originating incident. Synonyms: first incident, triggering incident, original incident, source incident.

terms.name: 🧩 Fulfillment Team
terms.description: The team assigned to work this ITIL record. Primary dimension for team-level workload and performance analysis. More granular than Organization, more aggregate than Assigned Resolver. Use to identify which teams have the highest backlog, longest MTTR, or lowest FCR. Source field by record type: Incident = assignment_group, Problem = assignment_group, Change = assignment_group. Synonyms: team, group, assignment group, resolver group, support team, which team.

terms.name: 🧩 Has Linked Change
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this incident record has a linked Change ID indicating the incident may have been caused by or related to a change. Sum([Has Linked Change]) shows how many incidents are connected to change activity — a high ratio suggests change-induced incidents and is a key DORA signal. Synonyms: linked to change, change-induced, has change, associated change, change related.

terms.name: 🧩 Has Linked Problem
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Dual(Yes/No) — Yes when this incident record has a linked Problem ID indicating the incident has been associated with a root cause investigation. Sum([Has Linked Problem]) shows the volume of incidents tied to known problems. Useful for understanding what percentage of the incident backlog has a systemic root cause being addressed. Synonyms: linked to problem, has problem, associated problem, connected to root cause.

terms.name: 🧩 ITIL Record
terms.description: The parent concept for all three ITIL 5 practice area record types managed in the Service Intelligence accelerator. An ITIL Record represents a discrete unit of work in service management. There are three subtypes: Incident (something broke and needs fixing), Problem (root cause investigation to prevent recurrence), and Change (planned modification to IT infrastructure or services). All three share common dimensions including Priority, Business Impact, Resolution Urgency, Affected Service, Organization, Fulfillment Team, and the five conformed date fields (Opened Date, Started Date, Mitigated Date, Resolved Date, Closed Date). In the Service Intelligence application all three record types are combined into the ITIL_Facts table with Record Type as the discriminator field.

terms.name: 🧩 ITIL_MAGIC
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The auto-detecting pipeline application in the ITIL 5 Accelerator RAW layer. ITIL_MAGIC automatically determines whether to run a full load (first run, no QVD exists) or an incremental load (subsequent runs, QVD exists and watermark is available). On incremental runs ITIL_MAGIC queries the source API for only records updated since the watermark, merges them with the existing QVD using WHERE NOT EXISTS, removes deleted records using INNER JOIN, advances the watermark, and writes telemetry to the Meta QVD. This self-managing pipeline runs forever without manual intervention. Synonyms: pipeline app, ETL app, data loader, magic pipeline, ITIL pipeline.

terms.name: 🧩 Incremental Load
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: A reload strategy that only fetches records updated since the last successful run rather than reloading the entire dataset. In the ITIL 5 Accelerator ITIL_MAGIC automatically detects whether to run a full or incremental load based on whether a RAW QVD already exists. Incremental loads use the Watermark timestamp as the lower bound for the API query and merge new records with existing QVD data using WHERE NOT EXISTS pattern. A deletion handling pass using INNER JOIN removes records that were deleted in the source system. Incremental loads run in seconds rather than minutes, dramatically reducing API load on ServiceNow. Synonyms: delta load, partial load, incremental refresh, delta refresh, change data capture.

terms.name: 🧩 Last Updated Date
terms.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ITIL record in ServiceNow. Used by ITIL_MAGIC as the watermark comparison field for incremental loads — MAX Last Updated Date = current watermark. Source field by record type: Incident = sys_updated_on, Problem = sys_updated_on, Change = sys_updated_on. Synonyms: last modified, updated date, sys_updated_on, last changed, last touched.

terms.name: 🧩 Lifecycle Status
terms.description: The current lifecycle state of an Incident record in ITIL 5 terms. Conformed from the native ServiceNow state field into business-friendly labels: New, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, Closed, Canceled. Use Lifecycle Status as the primary status dimension in Service Intelligence — it works across all three practice areas. For incident-specific status values use the native Problem Status or Change Status fields. Selecting Is Active = Yes is equivalent to filtering Lifecycle Status to open states. Synonyms: status, incident state, current state, open or closed, ticket status, where is it.

terms.name: 🧩 Linked Change
terms.description: The Change ID linked to this problem record indicating a change is being implemented to resolve the root cause. Provides forward traceability from problem to resolution change. Synonyms: linked change, resolution change, fix change, associated change.

terms.name: 🧩 Linked Change ID
terms.description: The sys_id of the Change record linked to this Incident. When populated this may indicate the incident was caused by or related to a change. The Has Linked Change flag is the binary indicator. High volumes of incidents with Linked Change IDs is a DORA change failure signal. Synonyms: associated change, related change, change link, caused by change ID.

terms.name: 🧩 Linked Problem ID
terms.description: The sys_id of the Problem record linked to this Incident. When populated this field connects an incident to its root cause investigation. The Has Linked Problem flag is the binary indicator. Use Linked Problem ID to join incident records back to the Problems table to see the full problem context alongside incident data. Synonyms: associated problem, parent problem, root cause ID, problem link.

terms.name: 🧩 MRCM
terms.description: CALENDAR INTELLIGENCE: Most Recent Complete Month — a Dual(Yes/No) period flag that is Yes for all dates in the last fully completed calendar month. Unlike CMTD which is a partial month in progress, MRCM is a complete and stable period ideal for reporting and benchmarking. Use MRCM when you want to report on last month's full performance. Example: Resolved Date MRCM = Yes shows all records resolved in the most recently completed calendar month. Available on all five conformed date fields. Synonyms: last month, most recent complete month, prior complete month, last full month, completed month, previous month.

terms.name: 🧩 MasterCalendar
terms.description: CALENDAR INTELLIGENCE: The MasterCalendar is a generated date dimension table built in the Conform Data application using AUTOGENERATE and a While loop. It spans all dates covered by the data and provides pre-calculated date grains (Year, Month, YearMonth, Week, Quarter) and six period flags (CMTD, PMTD, MRCM, PRCM, CYTD, PYTD) for every calendar date. Each conformed date field joins to the MasterCalendar via Floor([Date Field]) which strips the time component to match the calendar date. This single join populates all calendar grains automatically for every conformed date field in the ITIL_Facts table. The MasterCalendar is stored as Conform_Master_Calendar.qvd and loaded into the Conform Data application before the conformed facts. Synonyms: calendar table, date dimension, date table, time dimension.

terms.name: 🧩 Mitigated Date
terms.description: CONFORMED DATE: The date and time partial relief was applied — a temporary measure that reduces impact before the permanent resolution is in place. Nullable for all three record types — not all records reach a mitigation step. Source field by record type: Incident = escalation timestamp (when the incident was escalated indicating partial action taken), Change = Null() — only populated for Emergency changes where an interim measure was applied, Problem = workaround_communicated_at (when the workaround was communicated to affected users). In the Service Intelligence accelerator the gap between Mitigated Date and Resolved Date reveals how long a workaround or interim fix was in place before the permanent solution was delivered. Synonyms: workaround date, escalation date, partial fix date, interim resolution date, workaround applied, when mitigated, when workaround communicated, relief date.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date
terms.description: CONFORMED DATE: The date and time this ITIL record was created and the SLA clock started. This is the universal starting point for all time-based calculations across Incidents, Problems and Changes. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at (ServiceNow incident table), Change = opened_at (ServiceNow change_request table), Problem = opened_at (ServiceNow problem table). In the Service Intelligence accelerator this field is identical across all three practice areas — selecting a month on Opened Date filters Incidents, Problems AND Changes opened in that month simultaneously. Floor() is applied to strip the time component for MasterCalendar joining. Synonyms: created date, logged date, reported date, submission date, when opened, when created, when reported, when logged, start date, ticket date.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date CMTD
terms.description: Current Month To Date period flag derived from Opened Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes for all dates from the 1st of the current calendar month through today. Drop on a filter pane to let users select Yes/No. Use Sum([Opened Date CMTD]) in measures to count records opened this month. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at, Change = opened_at, Problem = opened_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date CYTD
terms.description: Current Year To Date period flag derived from Opened Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes for all dates from January 1st of the current year through today. Use with Opened Date PYTD for like-for-like year over year comparison. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at, Change = opened_at, Problem = opened_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date MRCM
terms.description: Most Recent Complete Month period flag derived from Opened Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes for all dates in the last fully completed calendar month. Stable complete period ideal for reporting. Use with Opened Date PRCM for month over month comparison of two complete periods. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at, Change = opened_at, Problem = opened_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date Month
terms.description: Calendar month derived from Opened Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual() field — displays Jan-Dec, sorts numerically 1-12. Use for monthly distribution analysis across all three practice areas. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at, Change = opened_at, Problem = opened_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Opened Date PMTD
terms.description: Prior Month To Date period flag derived from Opened Date via MasterCalendar join. Dual(Yes=1/No=0) — Yes for the same elapsed day range in the prior month as CMTD covers in the current month. Use with Opened Date CMTD for like-for-like month over month comparison. Source field by record type: Incident = opened_at, Change = opened_at, Problem = opened_at.

terms.name: 🧩 Performance Flag
terms.description: PERFORMANCE FLAG: Binary Dual() indicator built as If(condition, Dual('Yes',1), Dual('No',0)). The text value 'Yes'/'No' displays in filter panes and charts. The numeric value 1/0 enables Sum([Flag]) for fast KPI calculations without Count(If()) set analysis. Every Performance Flag in the Service Intelligence accelerator follows this same pattern. Selecting 'Yes' on any flag filters all charts to matching records instantly. This term is the parent concept — all specific flags in this category are subtypes of Performance Flag.

terms.name: 🧩 Pipeline Pulse
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The pipeline observability dashboard application in the ITIL 5 Accelerator suite. Pipeline Pulse reads Meta QVDs (Meta_Incidents.qvd, Meta_Problems.qvd, Meta_Changes.qvd) which are written by ITIL_MAGIC after every reload with telemetry including record counts, API response times, merge durations and watermark values. Because the Meta QVDs use CONCATENATE loading with FileList() wildcards, the audit log grows automatically with every reload run — a permanent self-growing history of every pipeline execution. Pipeline Pulse answers the question: how did this data get to my application and when was it last refreshed? Synonyms: pipeline dashboard, telemetry dashboard, data freshness dashboard, reload history, pipeline monitoring.

terms.name: 🧩 Priority
terms.description: The overall priority level of this ITIL record combining Business Impact and Resolution Urgency. Values follow the ITIL 5 standard P1-P5 scale: P1 Critical (immediate response, major business impact), P2 High (urgent response required), P3 Moderate (standard escalation), P4 Low (scheduled resolution), P5 Planning (monitored, no immediate action). Priority drives SLA targets, escalation thresholds and reporting. Use Priority Sort Order for correct P1-P5 chart axis ordering — Priority as text sorts alphabetically (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5) which happens to be correct, but Priority Sort Order (1-5 integer) is the reliable sort key. This field is shared across all three practice areas — selecting P1 in a filter pane shows P1 Incidents, Problems AND Changes simultaneously. Synonyms: severity, urgency level, ticket priority, escalation level.

terms.name: 🧩 Priority Sort Order
terms.description: A sort-safe integer companion to the Priority field. Values: 1=P1 Critical, 2=P2 High, 3=P3 Moderate, 4=P4 Low, 5=P5 Planning. Always use this field as the sort dimension on Priority charts to guarantee correct P1-P5 ordering on chart axes. Never use Priority Sort Order as a display dimension — use Priority for display labels and Priority Sort Order for axis sorting only.

terms.name: 🧩 QVD
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: Qlik's proprietary binary file format for storing data with embedded field-level metadata. QVDs read at RAM speed — orders of magnitude faster than live database queries. Optimized incremental loads only scan new records by comparing watermark timestamps rather than re-reading entire tables. COMMENT FIELD metadata written at STORE time is embedded in the QVD and travels with the file to any downstream application. Invented by Qlik in 1993 — predates what competitors now rebrand as medallion architecture, data mesh and QVD layering. In the ITIL 5 Accelerator all inter-layer communication happens via QVDs: RAW writes QVDs, CONFORM reads and writes QVDs, VISUALIZE reads QVDs. Synonyms: QVD file, Qlik data file, data file, binary data store.

terms.name: 🧩 RAW Layer
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The first layer of the ITIL 5 Accelerator pipeline. Loads data directly from source systems using REST connectors with no transformation applied. Field names are native to the source system (e.g. opened_at, work_start, sys_id). The RAW layer exists purely to enable fast incremental QVD loads and to preserve source data fidelity. Applications in this layer: ITIL_MAGIC. Output: Incidents.qvd, Problems.qvd, Changes.qvd stored in lib://ServiceNow:DataFiles/ITIL/. The RAW layer should never be queried directly by visualization applications. Synonyms: raw data, source layer, extraction layer, landing layer, bronze layer.

terms.name: 🧩 Record Type
terms.description: The ITIL 5 practice area discriminator field that identifies which type of record each row represents in the ITIL_Facts concatenated table. Values: 'Incident' (unplanned service interruption), 'Problem' (root cause investigation), 'Change' (planned modification). This is the only field introduced in the Service Intelligence visualization layer — every other field travels from the CONFORM layer. Use Record Type in filter panes to isolate practice-specific views. In Qlik, Count([Incident ID]) automatically excludes Problem and Change rows because NULLs are ignored by COUNT — set analysis is not required. Synonyms: practice area, record category, ITIL type, ticket type, work type.

terms.name: 🧩 Resolution Urgency

Source field by record type: Incident = urgency, Problem = urgency, Change = urgency. Synonyms: urgency, how urgent, time sensitivity, resolution urgency.

terms.name: 🧩 Resolved By

Synonyms: resolved by, who fixed it, resolver name, who resolved it.

terms.name: 🧩 Resolved Date

NOTE: Resolved Date differs from Closed Date — resolution means the work is done, closure means the record was formally signed off. A record can be resolved but not yet closed. In the Service Intelligence accelerator MTTR = Resolved Date minus Opened Date. Synonyms: resolution date, fix date, work end, work completed, when resolved, when fixed, when completed, implementation end, restoration date, MTTR end date, resolved_at, work_end.

terms.name: 🧩 VISUALIZE Layer
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The third and final layer of the ITIL 5 Accelerator pipeline. Reads conformed QVDs only — no transformation logic, no source system connections, no field renaming. The VISUALIZE layer contains pure presentation logic: concatenating the three conformed QVDs into the ITIL_Facts table, creating the Record Type discriminator, and building charts and dashboards for end users. Applications in this layer: Service Intelligence, Pipeline Pulse. Because this layer reads only conformed QVDs, the same visualization application works regardless of which source system the data came from. Synonyms: visualization layer, presentation layer, gold layer, reporting layer, dashboard layer.

terms.name: 🧩 Watermark
terms.description: PIPELINE AND GOVERNANCE: The MAX updated timestamp from the previous successful reload stored in the Meta QVD (e.g. Meta_Incidents.qvd). Used as the lower bound filter for the next incremental API query — only records updated after the watermark are fetched. The watermark advances automatically after every successful run. If a reload fails the watermark does not advance, ensuring no records are missed. The watermark is calculated from the actual data loaded (Max([updated_on])) not from the reload clock, protecting against late-arriving records. Synonyms: high water mark, last loaded timestamp, delta timestamp, last updated timestamp, sync point.

categories.name: Calendar Intelligence
categories.description: Date grain and period flag concepts derived from the MasterCalendar. Explains how conformed date fields get Year, Month, YearMonth, Quarter and period flags (CMTD, PMTD, MRCM, PRCM, CYTD, PYTD) joined automatically. categories.name: Classification and Routing
categories.description: Shared dimension fields working identically across Incidents, Problems and Changes in the concatenated ITIL_Facts table. Selecting Priority, Affected Service, Organization or Fulfillment Team filters all three practice areas simultaneously with no additional configuration.

categories.name: Conformed Date Fields
categories.description: The five conformed date fields identical across Incidents, Problems and Changes. Each term documents which source system field maps to the conformed name.

categories.name: ITIL 5 Core Concepts
categories.description: Foundational ITIL 5 framework terms defining the three core practice areas — Incident Management, Problem Management and Change Enablement — that form the backbone of the Service Intelligence accelerator.

categories.name: Performance Flags
categories.description: Binary Yes/No indicator fields built using the Qlik Dual() pattern: If(condition, Dual('Yes',1), Dual('No',0)). Text value displays in filters and charts. Numeric value enables Sum(Flag) for rate calculations without Count(If()) gymnastics. Every flag has a corresponding master measure.

categories.name: Performance KPIs
categories.description: Measured ITIL 5 outcomes quantifying service management performance. MTTR, FCR Rate, SLA Compliance, Change Failure Rate, Known Error Rate and more. Each KPI is pre-built in the CONFORM layer using the Dual() flag pattern enabling Sum() aggregation without set analysis.

categories.name: Pipeline Observability

Distinct from the ITIL practice-area terms (Incident/Problem/Change); this category covers the "flight recorder" for the pipeline itself, sourced from the Pipeline Pulse app (Meta_*.qvd telemetry).

categories.name: Pipeline and Governance
categories.description: Architecture and operational terms describing how data moves through the ITIL 5 Accelerator pipeline from source system to visualization. Understanding these terms answers the question every analyst eventually asks: how did this data get to my application?

categories.name: Record Identity
categories.description: Fields that uniquely identify records and link the three practice areas together. Covers primary keys, human-readable numbers, URL links to source system records, and the relationship fields connecting Incidents to Problems and Changes.

categories.name: Source Systems

The Source System field makes the accelerator platform-agnostic — ServiceNow today, FreshDesk tomorrow, Numara or Remedy or Zendesk the day after. The CONFORM layer translates any source system into the same ITIL 5 field names.
